title: RWB-P6-E4040-CON: no custody operation, custody table, field types, notice column, decision code or rule id is specified for rwb-comms
source: Recovery Workbench TSD P6 Communications v2 T3.1, T3.2, T5.3, T6.1 and appendix T-A.1; Recovery Workbench FSD P6 Communications v3 A2.19; legacy RWB-E4-040 (Endpoints, Data, Screen and states, Permission checks)
section: 7 Acceptance criteria; 11 Data; 12.1 REST operations provided; 12.2 REST operations consumed; 12.3 Events published; 12.4 Events consumed; 14 Validation and messages; 15 Screens and states
description: FEAT-COM-06 asks that the Workbench track a physical document leaving and returning, and no source gives the elements that would carry it in the target. TSD P6 appendix T-A.1 lists eleven operations (API-P6-001 to API-P6-011) and none of them is a custody operation, and TSD P6 T3.1 holds notice, template, merge_field and signature_request and no custody table, so the two movement operations on the notice, the CustodyMovementRequest and Movement shapes and the notice-side movement reference column are fixed by RWB-P6-E4040-CON and their physical types are left to the baseline review. The legacy data table gives the custody row as DF-DOC-018 to DF-DOC-024, seven fields of which the seventh is not named, so the seventh element and the physical type of moved_at, from_location, to_location and held_by stand as the placeholder. The custody row and the document are P5's, and the custody write POST /documents/{documentId}/custody (API-P5-007) is the Ownership Map row that RWB-P6-E4040-APP records; no P5 contract story is named for this key, so the row is declared as consumed and faked with no C dependency. No source gives the decision code, the rule id, the eligible notice states, the location and holder vocabularies or the refusal texts of a movement, and the P6 requirement list holds no requirement for FEAT-COM-06, so the trace goes to the feature. The legacy permission and screen rows of this key (Litigation C and Litigation R, SCR-33 Template approval, and the two notice endpoints) describe the notice and template features and are not the rows of this feature, which is a conflict between the legacy story body and its own tables.
evidence: FSD P6 A2.19.1 to A2.19.4 name the outcome, the document hub and the roles only; TSD P6 T-A.1 ends at API-P6-011 with no custody operation; TSD P6 T3.1 lists four entities and no custody entity; TSD P6 T3.2 lists LOV-NOTICE, LOV-DELIVERY, LOV-SENT-TYPE and no movement list; TSD P6 T5.3 names NoticeGenerated, NoticeDispatched and NoticeDelivered and no custody event; TSD P6 T6.1 has no custody right; legacy RWB-E4-040 Data names DF-DOC-018 to DF-DOC-024 with one field unnamed, and its Endpoints, Permission checks and Screen and states name Litigation rights, SCR-33 and the two notice endpoints.
area: rwb-comms contract and notice data; rwb-document contract and custody data; decision record and reference data
owner_role: Tech lead of rwb-comms, with the rwb-document owner, the decision-library owner and the solution architect for the Ownership Map rows
proposed: Baseline the two movement operations, the seven-element Movement, the notice-side movement reference and the decision element as declared here; ask the rwb-document owner to publish the custody write and the document read and to plan the P5 contract story; keep the seventh element, the four physical types, the decision code, the rule id and the refusal texts as the placeholder until their owners name them; confirm each value at the consumer sign-off.
